interpretation: High PSNR/SSIM means the stego image looks like the cover; it does not prove resistance to steganalysis.
Low MSE is not a proof of security.
Exact extraction from an unmodified PNG does not establish robustness to lossy transforms.
Robustness, imperceptibility, capacity, speed and statistical undetectability are different objectives and trade off.
HUGO/WOW/S-UNIWARD minimise a distortion model; that is not a proof that no steganalyst can detect the message.
label: Educational experiment - not a live UAV transmission

metric_definitions.ber: (wrong bits + missing bits) / expected payload bits; 1.0 if extraction failed entirely
metric_definitions.capacity_bits_raw: algorithm capacity for this cover excluding the 128 bootstrap samples (estimated from the cover)
metric_definitions.capacity_bits_verified: largest payload actually embedded AND extracted exactly in a verification run (bytes x 8)
metric_definitions.embed_ms: sender-side codec.embed_frame duration (monotonic perf_counter); setup_ms = cost-map time inside it (STC methods)
metric_definitions.extract_ms: receiver-side PNG decode + bootstrap validation + extraction (perf_counter)
metric_definitions.mse: mean over all samples (pixels x channels) of (cover - stego)^2
metric_definitions.payload_bits: payload bytes x 8 (the complete payload: AEAD test envelope or synthetic fixture)
metric_definitions.psnr_db: 10 log10(255^2 / MSE); null when MSE = 0 (identical images, infinite PSNR)
metric_definitions.robustness: per attack: 'recovered' = full pipeline (bootstrap + payload) returned the exact payload; 'recovered_oracle_only' = only a direct extraction with the known algorithm/length/parameter was exact; 'partial' = oracle BER in (0, 0.1]; 'failed' = otherwise (BER ~0.5 is chance level). oracle_ber = BER of that direct extraction
metric_definitions.ssim: mean SSIM, uniform 7x7 window, K1=0.01, K2=0.03, L=255, data range 0..255, averaged over all windows and channels

payload_construction.key: TEST-ONLY key = HKDF-SHA256(public label) -- not secret, never used for UAV traffic, not displayed
payload_construction.note: The same AppWire bytes are embedded by every algorithm in this comparison. The live transport additionally wraps them in Frame v1 (12-byte header + 32-byte HMAC) bound to the algorithm id.
payload_construction.serialisation: UTF-8 message bytes -> ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD (header bound as associated data) -> AppWire v1
